falsification_prediction: The minimal experiment uses the existing DINO-WM Wall checkpoint and trajectories with identical CEM seeds, candidate population, horizon, and controller settings to compare full recomputation, RankSafe exact-prefix caching, and a negative-control cache that forcibly randomizes the action-dependency mask at the chosen boundary with fallback disabled for that control arm. The load-bearing variable is M_b, the binary action-dependency mask for the cached prefix: when M_b is correct, the cached and full runs should make the same CEM first-action choices and retain closed-loop success while native end-to-end planner latency decreases. Randomizing M_b while keeping the cache path and hit opportunity comparable should create candidate-cost rank inversions and lower first-action agreement and closed-loop success, rather than merely changing M_b itself. If exact prefix caching does not reduce native end-to-end latency, or if the randomized-mask control does not degrade downstream decisions, the planner-level invariance mechanism is falsified.
compute_budget: 2–4 A100 allocation, 12 A100-GPU-days total for graph instrumentation, CPU preparation, smoke checks, matched native latency, and closed-loop Wall evaluation; $0 API cost because the existing checkpoint and local trajectories are used; no full pretraining.
what_step_was_missed: C$^3$ache would have needed to identify and factor out the observation/history computation that is invariant across counterfactual CEM branches, then connect that exact reuse to a candidate-cost ordering and selected-action preservation test in the DINO-WM planner; its cross-chunk residual construction instead assumes smooth executed behavior and stops at task-success degradation.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: C$^3$ache reuses same-denoising-step residuals across smooth consecutive WAM chunks with negligible task-success degradation, whereas RankSafe factorizes the DINO-WM CEM forward graph at an exact action-independent observation/history prefix and certifies preservation of counterfactual candidate ordering and the selected action.

X-Cache gates cross-chunk block residual reuse with structure- and action-aware fingerprints and protects persistent KV updates, whereas RankSafe's reusable object is the exact shared prefix within one CEM candidate set and its acceptance condition is equality of planner-relevant computation, not a similarity threshold.

WorldCache adapts token skipping from curvature and drift to maintain rollout fidelity, whereas RankSafe leaves all action-conditioned suffix rollout computation intact and targets the distinct downstream quantity of CEM cost ordering and closed-loop first-action selection.

EfficientVLA combines layer pruning, visual-token selection, and temporal action-head feature caching in CogACT, whereas RankSafe changes no DINO-WM parameters or visual tokens and reuses only the exact observation/history prefix shared by counterfactual Wall-planning candidates.

DINO-WM supplies the latent visual dynamics and test-time action-sequence optimization but does not define a reusable prefix object or a planner-level cache-validity condition, which RankSafe makes explicit and tests with native latency and closed-loop action agreement.

reviewer_concerns_and_responses.attack: Paper-pointed threat: openalex:W7172558534 (collision_hits). The Gate, Not the Cache reports that at skip ratio 0.9 on LIBERO-Object, reuse and deletion fall to 0.68 and 0.31 respectively versus dense 1.00 when the next gate is harvested from the model's own accelerated forward; the collapse is invisible to the evaluated action-level detectors. This threatens any cache whose validity signal is self-contaminated across control steps. RankSafe instead computes a full candidate canary under the deterministic contract, falls back on mismatch, and directly measures first-action agreement and closed-loop success, so the hit is a provenance threat already covered by the candidate's guard rather than exact-mechanism overlap.
